title: Dense matrix public performance audit
objective: Provide a machine-readable, reproducible correctness and performance audit of public dense matrix operations over ZZ, QQ, GF(2), GF(7), and a large word prime, with separated cold/warm measurements, backend traces, bounded routine mode, opt-in full Sage comparison, and a prioritized remediation handoff
references: SageMath public dense matrix behavior and performance

oracles: Sage.js explicit result witnesses and algebraic identities

handoff.summary: Added a machine-readable dense matrix audit with quick, routine, and full modes; verified 14 public operations over ZZ, QQ, GF(2), GF(7), and GF(2^61-1); separated process/bootstrap/first/warm timings; classified native routes; and compared representative workloads with SageMath.
risks: Cross-host timings are intentionally reported rather than ratcheted; retain reports on Linux x64, Linux arm64, and Darwin arm64.
GF(2^61-1) row/column swaps are public capability holes and most large-word-prime operations emit no backend trace.
The lane needed a local M4RI build because the shared parallel cache did not provision that package.
next_steps: Implement canonical arbitrary-word-prime storage with bulk range ingress, direct swaps, and traceable algorithms.
Replace selection-and-reconstruction swaps with direct exact/resource and packed operations.
Profile and batch GF(2) random fill.
